title: to_pdf reported success when it had written nothing
description: The PDF renderer only checked whether the target file existed. A stale PDF from a previous render satisfied that check, so a browser run that produced nothing reported success and the old document would have been published as the new one. The bug had been present for as long as the function, and every PDF in docs/ was produced through it.
resolution: Compares the file's modification time before and after rendering, and reports failure when nothing new was written. The output path is also resolved, since Chrome writes --print-to-pdf relative to its own working directory rather than the caller's. Covered by three tests.

title: The dashboard has no authentication
description: The browser interface is bound to 127.0.0.1 and has no auth by design. That was defensible when every action was pause or kill, but the same interface now approves plans, spends the budget cap and can push to every repository the configured token can see. Anyone who can reach the port can do all of it.

title: The README describes an older, smaller pipeline
description: README.md says the factory is six agents and describes the Coder as emitting a full codebase in one pass. There are eleven agents, and the Coder now reads, writes, runs the test suite and corrects itself. The docs/ papers and HANDOVER.md are current; the README is the entry point most people read first and is not.
